terms.gloss: a daring attempt, venture, undertaking or enterprise
terms.comment: Our preferred word for modern adventure when the emphasis is on something voluntarily and boldly undertaken. For ordinary family speech, prefer ausum when an ancient word is wanted.

A medieval Latin word connected with what happens, chance, fortune, risk or venture; retained here as a secondary word for modern adventure by later semantic extension, especially through the Romance development of the word. The English word adventure ultimately belongs to the adventūra family, but its cheerful modern sense is later than the core medieval Latin meanings. Use adventūra when the later European word-family itself is useful.

phrases.english: Let’s seek a new adventure today.
A new adventure awaits us; a modern-style use, not presented as an ancient idiom.

sources: Lewis & Short / Logeion: ausum · Mittellateinisches Glossar: adventura · Medieval legal glossary: adventura / adventurare / adventurarius
